intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding myelin protein zero (MPZ; 159440) on chromosome 1q23.3.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the MPZ gene, which encodes myelin protein zero.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe a family with a heterozygous mutation in MPZ, confirmed in two generations.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports CHN caused by a heterozygous MPZ mutation. The CHN2 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The MPZ gene is located on chromosome 1q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: the identification of a mutation in the gene (MPZ) for protein zero (P0)
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene named in the paper; not stated in the abstract itself.

paragraphs.text: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition with onset of hypotonia, paresis, and areflexia before birth, in the neonatal period, or in early infancy. On histopathology, myelin sheaths are absent or thin. Most reported patients have died within the first years of life (Smit et al., 2008). Mutations had been described in the MPZ, EGR2, PMP22, and MTMR2 genes (Smit et al., 2008).

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition.
checks.evidence_quote: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition

checks.claim: In congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy, hypotonia, paresis, and areflexia begin before birth, in the neonatal period, or in early infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis and areflexia

checks.claim: On histopathology, myelin sheaths in congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy are absent or thin.
checks.evidence_quote: Histopathologically there are no or thin myelin sheaths.

checks.claim: Most reported patients with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy have died within the first years of life.
checks.evidence_quote: Most of the few patients described in literature die within the first years of life.

checks.evidence_quote: Mutations have been described in the following genes, MPZ, EGR2, PMP22, and MTMR2.

paragraphs.text: Mandich et al. (1999) described the clinical, morphologic, and immunohistochemical features of a patient with congenital hypomyelination. They characterized congenital hypomyelination as a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy with onset in early infancy, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severely slowed nerve conduction velocities. They reported that the patient's clinical features were quite distinct from those of CMT1B or Dejerine-Sottas syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Szigeti et al. (2003) reported a patient with congenital hypomyelination who had cranial nerve dysfunction, respiratory failure, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The cardiomyopathy confounded the clinical picture. Findings on muscle biopsy suggested that abnormal innervation affected muscle fiber differentiation in the early postnatal period.

paragraphs.text: Kochanski et al. (2004) described the clinical and morphologic features of a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy, which they characterized as a severe neuropathy with onset in early infancy. They noted that sural nerve biopsy in this disorder shows a characteristic picture of nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons, basal lamina onion bulbs, and no myelin breakdown products.

paragraphs.text: In the family with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy reported by Smit et al. (2008), the heterozygous MPZ mutation was confirmed in 2 generations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance. In isolated patients, Mandich et al. (1999) and Szigeti et al. (2003) found that the MPZ mutations had occurred de novo.

checks.claim: Transmission of the MPZ mutation in the congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy family reported by Smit et al. (2008) is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe a family with a heterozygous mutation in MPZ, confirmed in two generations.
checks.explanation: A heterozygous mutation found in two generations fits dominant transmission, but the abstract never says 'autosomal dominant'. It also gives no pedigree details, such as whether male-to-male transmission occurred.

paragraphs.text: Warner et al. (1996) suggested that CMT1B, Dejerine-Sottas syndrome, and congenital hypomyelination may not be separate pathophysiologic entities. Instead, they proposed that these disorders form a spectrum of related 'myelinopathies' caused by an underlying defect in myelination.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with congenital hypomyelination, Mandich et al. (1999) identified a de novo gln215-to-ter (Q215X) mutation in the MPZ gene. The authors concluded that this finding confirmed that congenital hypomyelination is allelic with the milder MPZ-related disorders CMT1B and Dejerine-Sottas syndrome.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy, Szigeti et al. (2003) identified a complex de novo mutation in the MPZ gene. The mutation consisted of a 3-bp deletion of CTA at nucleotides 550 to 552 and an insertion of G at nucleotide 550. Conceptual translation predicted that it would cause a frameshift.
